strategy:
1. Approach and rationale

Use harmonic-direction coordinate search with an exact one-dimensional minimization along each chosen direction. A direction is a zero-sum DCT-II mode, so moving along it preserves the required mass. Along any such line, every finite-support lag value is a quadratic polynomial in the line parameter. For the parent resolution and other small n, minimize the maximum of these quadratics by enumerating their pairwise intersections, stationary points, and feasible endpoints. Cycle through the modes, retaining only moves that improve the exact score. At larger n, use a bounded grid-and-refinement search along selected modes to control work. Add a few box-aware, multi-coordinate mass-transfer directions so the search can move when a candidate lies on many box faces. Use a small set of feasible starts and preserve the parent as a fallback.

This is materially different from the supplied program and all prior approaches in the context. It uses neither SLSQP or single-active-lag subgradients, nor a smoothed maximum, active-lag LP, threshold-accepting pair transfers and pair scans, or whole-vector differential evolution. Its central operation is a harmonic-direction line search that exploits the exact quadratic form of every lag restriction; it uses no gradient or surrogate objective.

The mathematical facts are that the nonconstant DCT-II modes have zero sum and span the sum-zero subspace, and that the maximum of finitely many quadratic lag functions on one feasible line can be minimized by checking its endpoints, active-function intersections, and stationary points. These facts make the small-n line minimization well specified, not the full problem convex. The heuristic is that cycling through harmonic scales and using additional starts may improve the supplied construction by exploring directions that the parent’s local solver did not exploit. Coordinate search is still local, and the larger-n grid line search is approximate. Do not claim a global optimum, a guaranteed improvement, or attainment of 0.3808.

2. Mathematical specification

For the selected integer n in 1 through 999, let dx = 2/n, S = n/2, and h be a real vector of length n. The feasible set is 0 <= h[i] <= 1 for every zero-based index i and sum_i h[i] = S. For each integer lag s from -(n-1) through n-1, define p_s = max(s,0), r_s = max(-s,0), and m_s = n - abs(s). The exact finite-support lag value and score are

q_s(h) = dx * sum over j=0,...,m_s-1 of h[p_s+j] * (1-h[r_s+j]),
C(h) = max_s q_s(h).

There are exactly 2n-1 lag values. This is the linear, truncated-overlap correlation and equals max(np.correlate(h, 1-h, mode='full') * dx). Include both lag directions. Do not use circular correlation or replace a truncated overlap by an identity involving the full integral of h. The products make the full minimax objective generally nonconvex.

For k=1,...,n-1, use the DCT-II direction v_i = cos(pi*k*(i+0.5)/n), for i=0,...,n-1. Each direction has sum zero in exact arithmetic; together they span the sum-zero subspace. Subtract the computed mean and correct the last entry by the residual sum to limit floating-point drift, then normalize to max_i abs(v_i)=1. For an optional box-aware direction, select disjoint donor coordinates with h[i]>0 and receiver coordinates with h[i]<1, assign negative and positive weights respectively, and scale the two groups to equal total magnitude; this also gives sum(v)=0.

For any nonzero zero-sum direction v, the complete feasible interval for alpha is [lo,hi]. Initialize lo=-infinity and hi=+infinity. For v[i]>0 update lo=max(lo,-h[i]/v[i]) and hi=min(hi,(1-h[i])/v[i]). For v[i]<0 update lo=max(lo,(1-h[i])/v[i]) and hi=min(hi,-h[i]/v[i]). Ignore exactly zero entries. The interval contains zero for a feasible h and is finite for a nonzero zero-sum v. Every h+alpha*v in that interval preserves the sum and box bounds.

For each lag s, write p=p_s, r=r_s, and m=m_s. Along that line,

q_s(h+alpha*v) = a_s + b_s*alpha + c_s*alpha^2,

a_s = q_s(h),
b_s = dx * sum_j [v[p+j]*(1-h[r+j]) - h[p+j]*v[r+j]],
c_s = -dx * sum_j v[p+j]*v[r+j].

Thus the exact restricted objective is F(alpha)=max_s(a_s+b_s*alpha+c_s*alpha^2). For a global minimum on the line, it suffices to examine lo, hi, each real pairwise intersection root of two lag quadratics, and each in-interval stationary point -b_s/(2*c_s) for a nonconstant lag quadratic. Between consecutive pairwise roots, the ordering of every pair of lag polynomials is fixed, so the upper envelope is one quadratic there; its minimum is an endpoint or its stationary point. This is an exact line-search characterization, not a convexity claim about C(h). For larger n, use a finite grid and refinements of this same F(alpha); that is a restricted search heuristic, and the original exact score judges every materialized candidate.

3. Implementation procedure

3.1. Program structure. Write a complete program defining run(seed=42, **kwargs) at top level. Use NumPy and math only unless another allowed library is genuinely needed; no solver is needed. Define all helpers at top level with explicit arguments, including n. Do not use closures, lambdas, mutable global optimization dimensions, filesystem or network access, or parallel workers. Use float64 arrays. Implement separate helpers for resolution and parent handling, capped-simplex projection, feasibility checking, lag values and exact score, direction creation, line coefficients, quadratic roots, line candidate generation, one line search, one sweep, and run. Do not redefine, serialize, reconstruct, or hard-code initial_h_values. The pre-imported evaluate_erdos_solution need not be called because the program must implement the stated score itself.

3.2. Select the resolution and establish fallbacks. Attempt to read initial_h_values from the runtime globals, flatten it to a float64 vector, and accept it as a parent source only if its length is 1..999, every entry is finite, and all entries are within [-1e-8,1+1e-8]. Use it directly as the first start when feasible; copy only as needed to avoid mutating the supplied array. A finite parent that is slightly outside the box within this tolerance must be projected before use. Reject a parent with a materially out-of-range entry.

Accept kwargs['n_points'] only when it is a non-boolean scalar representing an exact integer in 1..999. Use that n if valid; otherwise use the valid parent length, or n=47 if no valid parent exists. If a valid parent has a different length from the selected n, interpolate it at normalized cell centers: old positions are (i+0.5)/old_n, new positions are (j+0.5)/n, and values beyond the old center range are held at the nearest endpoint. Project the transferred vector onto the selected feasible set. This projected vector is the parent-derived fallback at that resolution; compare scores only at the selected n. If parent conversion, interpolation, or projection fails, mark the parent unavailable. Independently create the constant vector 0.5, which is feasible for every allowed n.

Create a NumPy Generator from int(seed); if conversion or construction fails, use seed 42. Never mutate the pre-imported parent. For n=1, return [0.5] and its exact score directly.

3.3. Implement feasibility, projection, and exact score. Define is_feasible(h,n) to require shape (n,), finite entries, bounds within 1e-12 of [0,1], and absolute sum error no greater than 5e-10*max(1,n). Before scoring, repair any candidate outside the exact box or with sum error greater than 5e-12*max(1,n) using the projection helper; discard it if repair fails. Returned projections must have entries in [0,1].

The Euclidean projection onto the capped simplex has the form h[i]=clip(z[i]-lambda,0,1), where lambda is chosen so the sum is S. In project_capped(z,n), reject a wrong shape or nonfinite input, convert to float64, and cap the temporary input to [-1e6,1e6]. Set lo=min(z)-1 and hi=max(z); their clipped sums are n and zero. Perform 80 bisection steps, moving lo upward when sum(clip(z-mid,0,1))>S and moving hi downward otherwise. Form h with the midpoint. Correct the residual S-sum(h) in index order, adding at most 1-h[i] for a positive residual or subtracting at most h[i] for a negative residual. Stop when the residual is at most 5e-13*max(1,n). Reject a nonfinite result, a box violation beyond 1e-12, or a sum error beyond 5e-10*max(1,n). This projection jointly enforces the box and sum; never clip and then rescale.

The exact score helper first validates feasibility. Compute q=np.correlate(h,1.0-h,mode='full')*(2.0/n), require length 2n-1 and finite values, and return its unrounded maximum as a Python float. Return positive infinity for an invalid candidate. If the correlation call raises, recover by summing the explicit q_s formula over all 2n-1 lags; this is the same finite-support objective. Do not clamp, round, or substitute a smoothed or surrogate score.

3.4. Construct starts and directions. Score and retain the parent fallback and constant fallback independently of the start limit. Build feasible start proposals algorithmically: parent first if available, a block vector, a projected Gaussian perturbation of the parent with standard deviation 0.08 if available, a cosine wave, and a seeded uniform [0,1] vector. Without a parent, begin with the constant vector, followed by the block, wave, and uniform proposals. The block has its first floor(n/2) entries equal to 1, its next entry equal to 0.5 when n is odd, and all remaining entries zero. The wave has entries clip(0.5+0.45*cos(2*pi*(j+0.5)/n),0,1). Project every proposal, discard failures, and remove duplicates if max_i abs(a[i]-b[i])<1e-8. Keep the parent as the first search start when available. Score all feasible proposals exactly and register any improvement even if it is not selected as a start; use the start caps in section 4, retaining the parent-first order.

Build DCT modes using the formula in section 2. Check finiteness, remove any numerical mean, correct the residual sum, and normalize by the largest absolute entry. Randomize their processing order with the seeded generator each sweep. Also create the section-2 box-aware direction at the current h for each requested group direction: choose disjoint eligible donors and receivers in a seeded random order, use positive random weights, normalize donor and receiver totals to one, assign negative donor and positive receiver entries, and normalize max absolute value to one. Reduce the group size or omit the direction if distinct eligible groups cannot be formed. These directions are line-search directions, not separate transfer proposals.

3.5. Implement one line search. Given feasible h, its current exact score, and a finite zero-sum direction v, compute [lo,hi] from the coordinate bounds. Skip the direction if the interval is nonfinite, inconsistent, or narrower than 1e-12. Compute A=(a_s), B=(b_s), and D=(c_s) for every lag using the formulas in section 2; use q from the exact lag-values helper for A and slice dot products for B and D. Reject the direction if any coefficient is nonfinite. Do not construct a dense lag-by-coordinate Jacobian.

For n<=64, generate the exact critical-point set: lo, hi, zero, every finite stationary point -b_s/(2*c_s) in the interval when c_s is nonzero, and every real root in the interval of (a_s-a_t)+(b_s-b_t)*alpha+(c_s-c_t)*alpha^2=0 for each s<t. Implement a top-level quadratic-root helper. Treat a sufficiently small quadratic coefficient as a linear equation; if both leading coefficients are negligible, return no isolated root. For a quadratic, tolerate only a small negative discriminant due to roundoff, set that to zero, and use a stable q-formula for the two roots. Discard nonfinite roots and retain roots only within the interval up to a tolerance of 1e-10*max(1,abs(lo),abs(hi)); clip tolerated roots to the interval. Sort and merge near-duplicate alpha values with that same scale-aware tolerance. Endpoints and zero must remain candidates.

Evaluate F(alpha)=max_s(A_s+B_s*alpha+D_s*alpha^2) for this critical-point list in chunks of at most 512 alpha values, not in one large candidate-by-lag matrix. The pairwise intersections partition the interval into regions with a fixed active quadratic, so the smallest F among this list is the exact mathematical line minimum. The polynomial values are the exact line restriction of the original lag objective, not a smoothed surrogate.

For n>64, use a bounded grid on [lo,hi] rather than enumerating all pair intersections. For 65<=n<=256, begin with 33 equally spaced points and zero, identify up to three distinct local-minimum grid cells, and refine each cell for four rounds using nine equally spaced points per round. For 257<=n<=999, begin with 17 points and zero, identify up to two distinct cells, and refine each for three rounds using seven equally spaced points per round. At each round choose the lowest-F sampled point in a cell and make the next cell the interval between its neighboring sampled points; at a cell endpoint use the inward adjacent interval. Deduplicate sampled alpha values. This finite search does not assume the line function is unimodal.

In either branch, use the polynomial envelope to rank generated alpha values and materialize at most the section-4 number of lowest-F distinct candidates, ensuring zero and the best predicted alpha are included when capacity permits. For each materialized nonzero alpha, form h_trial=h+alpha*v, validate it, and project it only if floating-point error violates feasibility. Compute its score with the exact np.correlate-based helper. Compare it with the current point and choose the lowest exact score. Accept the line result only if its exact score is smaller by more than 1e-12; otherwise keep h. The polynomial envelope ranks line candidates, but no candidate is accepted or registered globally on that ranking alone.

3.6. Run bounded coordinate sweeps and maintain the best. Initialize global_best from the lowest exact score among the feasible parent fallback, when present, and the constant fallback. Score each feasible start and register it if it improves global_best by more than 1e-12. For each selected start, run one sweep. A sweep processes its selected DCT modes in seeded random order, updating the current feasible h after every accepted exact-score line move; then generate and process its box-aware group directions from the latest h. Recompute all line coefficients after each accepted move because h changed. A failed direction or exception skips only that direction. Keep the current trajectory separate from a copied global best, and update the latter only on an exact-score decrease greater than 1e-12.

After all starts, run the bounded global polishing sweeps in section 4 from a copy of global_best. Stop polishing early if a complete sweep produces no exact-score improvement. All starts, directions, line candidates, and sweeps are sequential and finite. A failed start, projection, coefficient calculation, or line search must not erase the global best or either fallback.

3.7. Finalize. Reproject the selected global best, validate it, and recompute its exact score. Revalidate and rescore the parent-derived fallback when available and the constant fallback. Choose the valid candidate with the lowest exact score at the selected n. If any final operation fails, choose the lowest-scoring valid fallback; the constant vector is the final recovery option. Return exactly (h_values,c5_bound,n_points), where h_values is a float64 NumPy vector of length n, c5_bound is its unrounded exact score, and n_points is the Python integer n.

4. Search choices and useful variations

Correctness requirements do not vary: evaluate all 2n-1 finite-support lags for exact scores; use a joint capped-simplex projection; keep all scored and returned candidates feasible; use exact scores for acceptance and final selection; and preserve a validated parent-derived fallback whenever possible. Never replace the original objective with a periodic or full-integral identity.

Use these defaults. For n<=48, process all n-1 DCT-II modes and two box-aware directions per sweep. For 49<=n<=64, process 24 distinct log-spaced DCT frequencies and two box-aware directions. For 65<=n<=256, process 12 distinct log-spaced DCT frequencies and two box-aware directions. For n>256, process 8 log-spaced frequencies and one box-aware direction. Select log-spaced integer frequencies between 1 and n-1, include both endpoints, round to integers, and remove duplicates. The default parent has n=47, so its small-n search uses all 46 nonconstant modes and the exact critical-point line search.

Use at most 3 starts for n<=256 and 2 for n>256, including the parent or constant first start. Search each selected start for one sweep. Then allow at most two global polishing sweeps when n<=64 and one when n>64, stopping early after a sweep without an exact improvement. For exact critical-point lines, confirm at most 8 distinct low-envelope candidates with the exact score. For 65<=n<=256, confirm at most 4; for n>256, at most 2. Always include the current point in the comparison and do not score it again unnecessarily.

Bounded variations may use one to three polish sweeps for n<=64, one or two box-aware directions per sweep, or a different cosine phase and perturbation scale in 0.03..0.18. A coder may move the exact-line threshold within 48..72 only if the resulting candidate count and work remain bounded, or use 8..20 log-spaced modes for larger n. Use the stated settings as the default; all stopping and any result-dependent decisions must run inside run. Do not claim an untested parameter choice is superior or add an unbounded random search.

5. Numerical robustness and memory use

Use float64 and run sequentially on the one-CPU harness. Exact lag vectors use O(n) memory. The exact small-n line search can have O((2n-1)^2) critical alpha values; evaluate their envelopes in chunks of at most 512 by 2n-1 values. With n<=64 this is bounded and avoids a large temporary matrix. For larger n, use the bounded grid and refinements rather than enumerating all pairwise roots. Store only O(n) coefficient and candidate vectors, the selected O(n) direction list, and the small feasible-start set. Never build a dense (2n-1)-by-n Jacobian, Hessian, or quadratic solver matrix.

Use scale-aware tolerances for roots, reject nonfinite coefficients and roots, and ignore a failed pair-root computation while retaining endpoints and other candidates. If a direction has no feasible interval of useful width, skip it. If a candidate has roundoff-level infeasibility, restore both constraints with project_capped and then score the repaired candidate; discard it if repair fails. The exact score helper validates before scoring and uses the full finite np.correlate formula. A failed line, start, or score leaves the saved best unchanged.

Work is explicitly capped by n-dependent mode counts, start counts, line-grid sizes, exact-confirmation counts, and sweep counts. Coefficient construction and exact correlation are O(n^2) per selected direction or score; the large-n mode and confirmation caps keep this finite through n=999. Termination occurs after the stated sweeps or earlier when a full sweep has no exact improvement. If no search candidate improves, the validated parent fallback, or constant fallback when no parent is usable, remains available.

6. Runtime safeguards and return contract

The generated run function must check the optional resolution, parent shape and values, selected n in 1..999, seed conversion, and every candidate’s shape, finiteness, box bounds, and sum. Use joint projection for any feasibility restoration; do not clip and rescale separately. Compute the exact score from np.correlate(h,1.0-h,mode='full')*(2.0/n), with the equivalent explicit finite-lag fallback only if the correlation call fails. Every accepted candidate and every best/fallback comparison must use that exact score, not the polynomial ranking, a line-search approximation, or a score from another resolution.

Before returning, reproject and revalidate the selected vector, recompute its score from that returned vector, and compare it against retained valid fallbacks. If validation or scoring fails, use the best valid fallback and recompute its score. Return exactly the tuple (h_values,c5_bound,n_points), with n_points equal to len(h_values), h_values satisfying both constraints within floating-point tolerance, and c5_bound the corresponding unrounded evaluator score. These checks and calculations are source-code operations for the harness to execute; the coder only writes the program and does not calculate or verify a result while composing it.
